# Copilot Instructions

## Project Guidelines
- Prefer using `SystemTools.NativeTools.CopyWithRoboCopy` (robocopy-based copying) instead of manual `File.Copy`/recursive directory copy when copying files/folders in this solution.
- The project mission is to create a suite installer builder for enterprise deployment (Intune/SCCM). Suites can chain multiple MSI installs and perform packaging tasks (registry/file/env var/web extension changes, etc.). A key feature is a user-visible popup warning when a suite will close processes.
- The suite bootstrapper (SuiteSfxStub) extracts files with a specific directory layout: `Package/{id}/`, `Certificate/{id}/`, `File/{id}/`, `Executable/{id}/`, `PowerShell/{id}/`, `Registry/{id}/`, `BrowserExt/{id}/`, `Popup/`. The config file (`SuiteConfig.scfg`) sits at the extraction root, and `Suite.PathResolution.cs` resolves file paths against `_suiteRootDir` at runtime. SFX payload format: `[stubExe][zipBytes][int32 zipLength][int32 magic 'SUFX']`.
- The solution has a build-time conversion pattern in `SuiteBuilder.CreateSuiteExecConfig()`: UI model types (from SuiteCreatorAvalonia/SuiteCreatorModels) are converted to exec types (in SuiteOperations) at build time for both events AND packages. This ensures the serialized config JSON contains `$type` references to SuiteOperations assembly types, which the SuiteExecutor can resolve.
- Newtonsoft.Json serialization in the suite solution: `SuiteExecConfig.ToJson()` uses `TypeNameHandling.Auto` for polymorphic serialization at build time. At runtime deserialization in `Suite.LoadConfig()`, `EventConverter` and `PackageConverter` handle constructor injection (injecting `Log` and `List<RuleSet>`) into exec types that don't have default constructors. A two-pass deserialization is used: first pass (`SuiteExecConfigDto`) extracts RuleSets, second pass uses converters with those RuleSets. The SuiteExecutor project does NOT reference SuiteCreatorAvalonia — it can only access SuiteCreatorModels, SuiteOperations, Logger, MSITools, MSIxTools, SystemTools, and UserTools.
- The Visual Studio workspace root is the SuiteCreatorAvalonia folder (C:\Users\Keir\GitHubRepos\SuiteCreatorSolution\SuiteCreatorAvalonia\). When creating or referencing files in sibling projects (e.g., SuiteExecutor, SuiteOperations, SystemTools, Logger, etc.), use the `../` prefix for relative paths (e.g., `../SuiteExecutor/Suite.cs`). Without the prefix, files will be incorrectly created inside the SuiteCreatorAvalonia project directory.

## Code Style
- Prefer fully typed local variables instead of using `var` (except where explicitly needed). This preference applies specifically to the Suite enterprise installer-builder project context.
- Prefer class-level/global variables (fields) to be named using underscore-prefixed camelCase (e.g., `_exampleVariable`) rather than PascalCase (e.g., `ExampleVariable`).
- Prefer splitting large `Suite` class into focused `partial` class files (e.g., `Suite.Detection.cs`, `Suite.Registry.cs`, `Suite.Logging.cs`, `Suite.Mutex.cs`, `Suite.Execution.Package.cs`) to keep related logic grouped while retaining access to private fields. Package-related execution methods belong in their own partial file separate from event/stage orchestration.
- Place private methods below all ObservableProperty declarations in view model files.
- If an applicable using statement is at the top of the file, do not use the fully qualified type name (e.g., System.Threading.Tasks.Task); just use the short type name (e.g., Task).
